clue.text: A merry man, one said to be cooking food

indicators.note: 'said' means we only hear the words for one cooking food, so the spelling can change

blocks.note: a fryer is one cooking in hot fat; spoken, it matches a monk's title
tuck is British school slang for food, especially snacks

explanation.surface: One of Robin Hood's band is reputed to be the outlaws' cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The merry men are Robin Hood's outlaws in Sherwood Forest; this one is the jolly monk of the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the portly monk among Robin Hood's band of outlaws, traditionally called his merry men.

clue.text: Part of the army once more deposing one president

indicators.note: to depose is to remove from office, so the following item is thrown out of the phrase before it

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a straightforward synonym
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Soldiers rise up again to overthrow a head of state in a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing' suggests a coup against the president, but it only removes the Roman one from the word for once more; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan served as the fortieth leader of the United States, from 1981 to 1989.

clue.text: Shrewd as Pharaoh, the leader of Egypt

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: taken as written
Tutankhamun, the boy king, is commonly shortened to Tut
the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: Someone is praised as being as clever as an ancient Egyptian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person with sharp practical judgement who is hard to fool.

clue.text: The first religious believer

blocks.note: taken as written
1st written with the figure one as a letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is hailed as the earliest person of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the numeral 1 as the letter I turns the abbreviation 1st into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist holds that a god or gods exist, the core conviction of most faiths.

clue.text: Excited choirs arrive in the St Austell area

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of all three words together are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Thrilled singers turn up at a Cornish town for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: St Austell is a town on the south coast of Cornwall, England's far south-western county; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish Riviera is the tourist name for Cornwall's southern coast around St Austell Bay, with its mild climate and beaches.

clue.text: One unfairly blamed as the first to smear cloak with butter

indicators.note: 'the first' of a word is its opening letter, and only that one is kept here

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a cape is a sleeveless cloak
a butter here is something that butts, as a goat does with its horns

explanation.surface: Someone is wrongly accused of starting a smear campaign, or of spreading butter on a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is read as one who butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person made to carry the blame for the faults of others.

clue.text: This luxury accommodation is the tops

definitions.text: This luxury accommodation is the tops

blocks.clueFragment: This luxury accommodation is the tops
blocks.note: surface reading: some lavish lodging is the very best there is
setter's reading: the accommodation sits literally at the top of a building

explanation.surface: A glowing review of a smart hotel suite as simply the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tops' is slang for excellent, but here it also means physically highest.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is an expensive apartment occupying the highest floor of a tall building.

clue.text: Act of resistance no problem for army command

blocks.note: to make a stand is to resist
something easy poses no difficulty

explanation.surface: Defiance comes effortlessly to a military order.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers given this order on parade may relax their posture more than at ease.

clue.text: Stress I had to avoid mishap

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping it out, so those letters must be taken away

blocks.note: a mishap is a minor accident
'I had' contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure tries to steer clear of mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ID from the middle of ACCIDENT leaves ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent and stress both mean the emphasis placed on a syllable when speaking.

clue.text: Rousing slogan, but be in tears after fight

indicators.note: 'after' places one item behind the other, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a battle is a fight
to weep

explanation.surface: An inspiring motto still leaves someone weeping after a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle cry is a shout or phrase used to rally supporters to a cause.

clue.text: Offspring holding beer mug? Exactly

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so the second part sits within the first

blocks.note: a son is a child
a pot is an old word for a drinking vessel, as in pot of ale

explanation.surface: A child clutching a tankard, and someone confirms that is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British informal for precisely correct, used as an exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: Great to adhere mostly to soft drink

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange drink
to adhere is to stick

explanation.surface: Someone urges sticking with a fizzy drink as a fine idea.
explanation.walkthrough: STICK loses its final K and is attached to FANTA, the 'to' showing where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are casual praise for something wonderful or extremely good.

clue.text: Fail to deal with troubled region

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Authorities neglect an area beset by unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore a problem is to pay it no attention and leave it unaddressed.

clue.text: Miscreant concerned with affirmation of will

blocks.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading
probate is the legal proving that a will is valid

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer takes an interest in the proving of a dead person's testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a scoundrel of bad character.

clue.text: Safety procedure needed when digging up pavement?

definitions.note: a clause describing the tool rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the routine for crossing a road safely from the pavement
second meaning, read literally: the power tool a roadworker uses to break up the edge of the footpath

explanation.surface: Workers breaking up a footpath must follow proper safety rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The kerb is the British spelling of curb, the edge of the pavement (sidewalk); the British road-safety code for children has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerb drill is the routine taught to British children: stop at the edge, look both ways, listen, then cross.

clue.text: Loaf, starter that may be needed for a simple meal

definitions.text: that may be needed for a simple meal

blocks.note: a tin is a British loaf baked in a rectangular tin
an opener is something that starts things off

explanation.surface: Bread and a first course are all you need for a modest supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' and 'starter' look like parts of the meal; a tin opener is the British name for a can opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick supper of beans or soup comes out of a can, so the gadget for opening one is required.

clue.text: I’m surprised breakdown organisation covers horse

indicators.note: a thing that covers another wraps round it, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British roadside rescue service
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that the roadside rescue service insures a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses sudden discovery or surprise, just as the phrase in the clue does.

clue.text: Past making an attempt

blocks.note: the indefinite article
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Someone is beyond trying any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe time gone by, as in years earlier.

clue.text: One may win over a king

definitions.note: a clause describing the card rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the single pip on a playing card or die
second meaning: the card that outranks a king in most games

explanation.surface: Someone might persuade a monarch to come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'win over' suggests charming a ruler, but it means beating one in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace counts as one and in most card games is the highest card, above the king.

clue.text: Ironing lessons outside school hours?

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: ironing is smoothing things level, and lessons are sessions of teaching
second meaning: adult courses held after the working day

explanation.surface: Someone signs up for adult tuition in how to press clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironing makes a surface flat and level, so the first word is read as making even, not as the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult education courses are often held after work, so they run once the school day is over.

clue.text: See 19
Half a US state is a source of metals

indicators.note: half of something means the rest is cut away, keeping only the front part

blocks.note: a state in the Pacific Northwest

explanation.surface: A claim that part of America is rich in mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock mined for the valuable metal it contains, such as iron or copper.

clue.text: See 5
Get computer going again with another kick?

definitions.note: a noun phrase where the answer is a verb; read as kick again

blocks.note: first meaning: restart a machine
second meaning: re- for again plus a boot, which is a kick

explanation.surface: A frustrated user gives the machine another thump to start it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reboot is to restart a device's operating system after shutting it down.

clue.text: Tree covering river bottom

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping round it, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: a common broadleaf tree
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tree overhangs the bed of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river bottom' looks like a riverbed, but 'bottom' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Breech is an old word for the buttocks, surviving in breech birth and breeches.

clue.text: Not straight, lads becoming wild animals

blocks.note: bi is short for bisexual, straight being slang for heterosexual
boys, male children

explanation.surface: Young men who stray from the straight path turn into beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bison are large shaggy wild cattle of North American plains and European forests.

clue.text: Some easier rambles in the mountains

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Walkers prefer gentler hikes up in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged range of peaks, from the Spanish word for saw.

clue.text: Exhausted oneself, but a few deliveries brought success

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
did it means succeeded

explanation.surface: A bowler worked too hard, though a short spell paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bowlers deliver balls in overs of six, so a few deliveries make one over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo it is to work or exert yourself too hard and wear yourself out.

clue.text: Carried over island

blocks.note: past participle of bear, to carry
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something was transported across to an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large landmass in Southeast Asia shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

clue.text: Nice black sheep perhaps one I particularly detest

blocks.note: a sheep is an example of a beast, French bête
Nice is a city in France, so the word for black is French

explanation.surface: A family outcast is the person someone loathes most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' with a capital is the French city, signalling French words; 'black sheep' wants to be an outcast but is split into black and sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire, literally black beast, is a person or thing someone especially dislikes.

clue.text: Shoot a ploughman

blocks.note: first meaning: a new stem growing from the base of a plant
second meaning: one who tills the soil

explanation.surface: An order to gun down a farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is a sprouting side stem of grass or cereal, and also a person who cultivates land.

clue.text: Sailor’s shanty remixed with Mac

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording into a new version, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A seafarer's song gets a modern makeover with a Scottish collaborator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor’s' reads as possessive, but the 's stands for 'is' and joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman is someone who sails a yacht, a kind of seafarer.
